Subject: HPCloud throughput & streaming SLOs — reserved capacity qualification

Hi Aisha / Erin / Matt —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared spec for sizing the reserved pool:

- Primary workload: live transcription + short generative responses for chat UI (mixed streaming + single-turn).
- Targets you mentioned: p95 single-turn latency <= 200 ms, streaming initial-token latency <= 120 ms, sustained concurrent streams target ~250 concurrent active streams during peak (burst to 600), and expected 18M tokens/day across regions.
- Typical prompt lengths: median request ~75 tokens, average streaming session ~12 tokens/sec for 30–120s.
- Availability need: 99.9% SLA on the endpoint, with automatic fallback to smaller model if capacity constrained.

Immediate asks from our side so we can give a concrete reserved throughput and GPU shortlist:
1) Confirm whether the 250 concurrent streams number is per region or global peak.
2) Share any preferred GPU constraints (e.g., procurement limitation to A100 only) or strict power/cost ceilings.
3) Any regulatory constraints requiring on-prem/private deployment for sensitive logs (we discussed no for now).

I've attached the SLO summary you emailed and a short questionnaire to clarify session distributions. Next step: if you confirm the three items above we will run a short tabletop sizing (we'll propose H100 vs A100 configs) and share an estimated reserved throughput and cost delta.

Attachments: hpcloud_slo_requirements.pdf (pdf, 82KB)

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sizing playback with Karthik the week of Sep 27 — can you share availability?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the context and the histogram — that was helpful. High-level synthesis and recommendation below (we'll attach the spreadsheet with the bench numbers):

Short summary (US region, 250 concurrent typical, bursts to 400):
- H100 (4x 80GB) pilot: estimate sustained: ~420 concurrent streaming sessions with p95 initial-token latency ~95–110 ms; single-turn p95 ~120–180 ms depending on prompt size. Estimated reserved throughput: 3.2M tokens/min.
- A100 (6x 80GB) pilot: estimate sustained: ~320 concurrent streaming sessions with p95 initial-token latency ~130–160 ms; single-turn p95 ~160–220 ms. Estimated reserved throughput: 2.1M tokens/min.

Interpretation: H100 shows ~25–30% headroom for streaming concurrency and materially better initial-token latencies; A100 can meet target but at ~50% more reserved capacity (GPU count) to reach similar headroom.

Recommended pilot (min viable reserved pool):
- US region: 4x H100 80GB (reserved) with autoscale headroom to +2 nodes for burst; fallback policy: when queueing > 200 ms beyond SLO, route to a quantized 8-bit variant (same model family) with an automated quality guardrail. Cost delta vs A100 baseline: ~+32% monthly infra cost for H100 pilot vs A100 pilot for equivalent headroom (spreadsheet attached).

Pilot plan & timeline:
- Bench window: Redwood to run controlled microbench on hosted infra week of Sep 28 (we'll use HP sample traces). If HP prefers dedicated hardware, we can mirror the run but need a 48-hour window.
- Deliverable by Oct 1: short bench report + recommended committed pool + fallback runbook.
- Procurement ask: target pilot decision by Oct 4 so we can lock pilot capacity for mid-October.

Attachments (sent): redwood_gpu_reco_20270928.xlsx (bench numbers and cost model), sample_kernels.csv

Next steps for HPCloud: share the (redacted) trace sample link in Drive and confirm whether procurement requires an all-A100 quote only. If they require A100-only options, we'll provide a compensating higher-count A100 config (6x) and the cost delta.

I'll join the playback call — propose Sep 29 10:00AM PT (30m). Marissa — can you send calendar invite?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
